decisions.quote: We report a preregistered conceptual replication and extension of You, Dörnyei, and Csizér (2016), who found a central motivational role for vision. We review essential considerations in structural equation modeling and discuss how the initial study addressed these, then describe a conceptual replication with a South Korean sample of secondary school learners of English (N = 1,297).
decisions.reason: This candidate target is already represented by shipped row input_row_index 534 (You; Dörnyei; Csizér, 2015, 'Motivation, Vision, and Gender: A Survey of Learners of English in China', doi_o: 10.1111/lang.12140). Crossref metadata for 10.1111/lang.12140 confirms that You, Dörnyei, and Csizér's Language Learning article (vol. 66, issue 1, pp. 94-123) was published online in October 2015 and in a 2016 print issue; the replicating abstract cites the 2016 print year and lacks a reference list because only the abstract text was available.

decisions.reason: In new replicon and infection experiments using MDBK DNAJC14-KO and rescue cells (Figs. 8 and 9), the authors empirically re-test and confirm the lower RNA replication efficiency of noncp BVDV NCP7 relative to cp CP7 mediated by temporal NS2-3 cleavage regulation as well as the DNAJC14-independence of cp pestiviruses proposed in Reference 14 (Lackner et al., 2004, J Virol 78:10765-10775, 10.1128/JVI.78.19.10765-10775.2004). This 2004 study is an independent earlier publication with a distinct experimental scope and author list from the sole shipped original (input_row_index 113, Lackner et al., 2005, J Virol 79:9746-9755, 10.1128/jvi.79.15.9746-9755.2005, Reference 15) and from sibling target 2 (Lackner, Thiel, & Tautz, 2006, PNAS, Reference 53).

decisions.reason: Through gene rescue experiments expressing isolated GST-Jiv90(WT) or GST-Jiv90(W39A) in MDBK and SK6 DNAJC14-knockout cell lines lacking endogenous full-length DNAJC14 (Figs. 5 and 6), the authors empirically re-test and confirm the specific mechanistic findings of Reference 53 (Lackner, Thiel, & Tautz, 2006, PNAS 103:1510-1515, 10.1073/pnas.0508247103) that the isolated Jiv90 domain is sufficient to activate the NS2 protease and that the DNAJC14 J-domain cochaperone function is not required for NS2 activation. This 2006 PNAS study is an independent original work distinct from the sole shipped row (input_row_index 113, Lackner et al., 2005, J Virol, Reference 15) and from sibling target 0 (Lackner et al., 2004, J Virol, Reference 14).
